ns2:section.sectionText: This course will cover Shakespeare?s plays and poems. We will especially examine the generic complexities of the ?problem comedies? and of such major tragedies as Othello and King Lear; and the political and cultural climates of performance affecting the plays, both in early modern England and beyond Shakespeare?s time and place. The ability of plays both to reflect and challenge the expectations of their cultural milieux is evinced in Paul Robeson?s black Othello of 1930 London, or director Vishal Bharadwaj?s ?half-caste? Othello figure in the Bollywood film Omkara. What do we make of Lear?s three daughters become sons, and samurai, in the Japanese film Ran? Or Wole Soyinka?s transformation of Macbeth into a satire on African despots in King Baabu? These interpretations not only take Shakespeare in new directions, but also invite us to reconsider elements of the original that might initially go unnoticed. Students should expect to spend significant time reading material, especially if they are unfamiliar with Shakespeare?s English
